source_findings.dispatch: Eager host dispatch is not GPU completion; retain stream/queue distinctions.
source_findings.benchmarks: Versionless ResNet/A100 throughput, fixed compilation gains/latencies, utilization and migration-duration ranges are not compatible measured evidence.
source_findings.ad: Forward AD is not universally constant-memory or unused for neural networks; saved values and Python graph lifetime are different.
source_findings.storage: NumPy has strides/dtypes; Tensor.to is not copy-on-write; synchronization is not a prohibition on stream concurrency.
source_findings.module: Registration uses __setattr__, parameters includes frozen leaves, buffers may participate in AD, and load_state_dict copies into a compatible hierarchy rather than reconstructing it.
source_findings.jax: Callable transforms are not exclusive to JAX. vmap is not multi-device distribution; jit does not universally remove all host costs, and pmap does not infer every intended collective.
source_findings.runtime: Blanket no-training claims for LiteRT and fixed op/binary/memory counts need version/build/operation boundaries. The old ONNX hub picture is not a current bidirectional conversion contract.
source_findings.training: The original anatomy fence omits setup and uses integer (32) for randint size. Six launches and backward=2x are assumptions, not observed CUDA events; S7 preserves the source and separately repairs/runs the CPU case.

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.decision: Retain the original framing in the source layer; execution, differentiation and hardware abstraction are taught in separate thematic chapters rather than a duplicate introductory page.

sections.heading: Three Framework Problems
sections.decision: The three-problem taxonomy organizes this source. Its mechanisms have named destinations; a taxonomy label is not an additional learned algorithm.

sections.heading: The Ladder of Abstraction
sections.decision: Tensor/library/compiler/runtime layers have explicit destinations. Edge's complete arena ledger and Workflow's executed ONNX/TensorFlow target conversions complete the comparison. The source 102 MB versus 10–15 GB ladder mixes state budgets and is not imported as a symmetric benchmark.

sections.heading: Execution Problem
sections.decision: Opening bridge only; the next source ranges carry the substantive execution mechanisms.

sections.heading: Why execution strategy matters: The memory wall
sections.decision: HBM movement versus arithmetic, bytes/FLOP and achieved/peak limits already have worked address/roofline cases. Do not treat generic wall language as a measurement.

sections.heading: The computational graph
sections.decision: Values, dependency edges and execution/capture graphs are distinguished. Backprop derives graph traversal and shared-branch sums; S8 connects capture to compiler visibility.

sections.heading: Three execution strategies
sections.decision: S8 retains eager/fusion/Dynamo and the full trace-failure source example with branch/cond/export controls. Workflow executes ONNX and SavedModel-to-Lite boundaries. Capture, export and target execution are distinct; no universal speedup table is adopted.

sections.heading: Quantitative principles of execution
sections.decision: Launch amortization, captured regions, memory traffic and total compilation cost are explicit worked mechanisms in current S8/S7. The serial Python-tax timeline and assigned cost-curve crossovers remain illustrative inputs, not benchmarks.

sections.heading: Frameworks for the edge: TinyML and micro-runtimes
sections.decision: The complete source decisions and TFLM primary material now explain model buffer/arena/device RAM, overlapping lifetimes and preparation peak, operator registration and kernel support. Explicit assigned layouts and phase budgets are checked; source footprint/power figures are not adopted as measured facts, and no firmware run is claimed.

sections.heading: Differentiation Problem
sections.decision: The chapter derives the chain rule and the scalar-loss/many-parameter reason for reverse AD; no extra definition-only page is needed.

sections.heading: Forward and reverse mode differentiation
sections.decision: Full original forward-mode code, Baydin graph and both complete trace tables, arbitrary seeds, JVP/VJP identity and an explicit HVP are integrated with numerical checks.

sections.heading: Framework implementation of automatic differentiation
sections.decision: Micrograd, saved values, graph lifetime and the complete MultiplyAdd source example are retained. Separate setup_context/JVP and broadcast/higher-order checks expose interface limits without silently editing the original.

sections.heading: Abstraction Problem
sections.decision: Bridge into tensor/device/operator abstractions; the concrete material is mapped below.

sections.heading: Data structures and tensor abstractions
sections.decision: The original tensor-memory-layout SVG accompanies C/F offsets, element/byte strides, transpose, slice spans and aliasing. Device movement and memory hierarchy have separate explanations. The original 3D placement figure now accompanies explicit logical coordinates, TP/DP/PP groups and global-batch calculation in the distributed overview; source storage inaccuracies are not adopted.

sections.heading: Core operations
sections.decision: Matmul operand shapes, elementwise/reduction work, layouts and memory-bound versus compute-bound limits have concrete examples. A backend name alone is not proof of equal numerical behavior or kernel performance.

sections.heading: nn.Module Abstraction
sections.decision: Parameters, buffers and module hierarchy are tied to the existing executable MLP rather than a second overview.

sections.heading: Automatic parameter discovery
sections.decision: The complete original parameter-registration example and explicit leaf/optimizer/container cases distinguish registration from differentiation and optimization.

sections.heading: Mode-dependent behavior
sections.decision: eval recursively changes mode flags but does not disable AD. Freeze/input-gradient behavior and no_grad are distinguished; the source's third-mode shortcut is qualified.

sections.heading: Hierarchical composition and serialization
sections.decision: ModuleList, tied ownership, state_dict contents, compatible reconstruction/load and freeze flags are worked through. Original ResNet/freezing variants remain in the complete source; repeated syntax is not a separate mechanism.

sections.heading: Framework Platform Analysis
sections.decision: The full original hook example and numerical derivatives are accepted in MLP. Platform framing is reconciled by Workflow's actual export and complete MLOps feasibility/lifecycle explanations, without an exclusive production-versus-research brand taxonomy.

sections.heading: TensorFlow: The graph-first production machine
sections.decision: TensorFlow 2 eager default, tf.function capture, saved variables/functions/signatures, restored differentiation and explicit endpoints are explained with full original source. Actual CPU save/load, class-free process and Lite conversion/invoke establish one target boundary, not automatic all-target portability or an AOT speed guarantee.

sections.heading: PyTorch: The eager research standard
sections.decision: Eager recording, module state and capture/export are already explained with failures and supported alternatives. The source's ecosystem ranking is not a capability limit.

sections.heading: JAX: The functional transformation engine
sections.decision: Accepted gradient transformations are supplemented by the full original counter/state/ref/rank/cache/scan/psum explanations and diagram. Actual CPU cases expose hidden state, specialization, abstract branches, carry shape, donation, committed placement and four-device column reduction versus single-device batching. Callable-transform exclusivity, blanket no-mutation/all-host-cost elimination and inferred pmap communication remain findings; no full JAX guide or GPU training claim.

sections.heading: Framework trade-offs under measurement
sections.decision: Current PyTorch, TensorFlow and JAX worked programs explain the state/capture and mathematical distinctions. Selection uses operators, shapes, runtime and measured constraints. The source Keras integer input_shape and JAX reused PRNG key are recorded findings; the flawed triple snippet is not presented as a verified comparison.

sections.heading: Runtime constraint map
sections.decision: Worked constraints replace a brand ranking: ONNX missing kernels and batch bounds, SavedModel methods/signatures and actual Lite conversion, Edge's fixed arena/operator ledger, and MLOps admission/isolation/cost cases. Versionless 1.2–3x/2–10x gains and fixed footprint/op counts are rejected.

sections.heading: Deployment Targets
sections.decision: Current ONNX/TensorFlow export and separate CPU Lite conversion, MCU arena/operator examples and target feasibility are explicit. Fixed 10 ms/50 KB limits, obsolete hub arrows and no-training claims are not universal contracts. Unreferenced FL/transfer native images are separately resolved as reference-only after complete destination comparison, not inserted into this paragraph.

sections.heading: Framework Selection
sections.decision: Opening framing; the actual criteria and evidence remain in the next source intervals.

sections.heading: The framework selection trade-off space
sections.decision: Workflow's iteration budget, S8 capture/flexibility, actual export/operator boundaries and MLOps/Edge cost-quality/resource cases explain the trade-offs. Hard feasibility filters precede performance ranking. The old TensorFlow variant/no-training table is not accepted as a current capability inventory.

sections.heading: Framework selection criteria
sections.decision: Operators/shapes/dtypes/conversion, software/runtime environment and physical memory/placement are separate worked filters. All current MLOps lines were read: release/rollback compatibility, admission/isolation and cost/quality constraints already provide lifecycle criteria. Fixed op counts/binaries, utilization and 3–6-month migration claims are rejected.

sections.heading: Development support and long-term viability assessment
sections.decision: The complete original exit-path paragraph is retained in Workflow as evaluation advice, not empirical community rankings. A fresh class-free SavedModel load and ONNX missing-kernel example demonstrate removed code dependencies versus remaining runtime/operator needs. Current MLOps ties compatibility, migration and costs to actual release identities.

sections.heading: Anatomy of a Training Step
sections.decision: The complete original anatomy fence is retained with a warning; a separate initialized and corrected CPU program performs the full step and verifies each update.

sections.heading: Phase 1: Forward pass (solving the execution problem)
sections.decision: 32×784→32×256→32×10 shapes, ReLU, mean cross-entropy and both forward mm events are worked through. Source launch-count assumptions are not measurements.

sections.heading: Phase 2: Backward pass (solving the differentiation problem)
sections.decision: All four parameter gradients and optional input derivatives are independently checked. Actual three versus four backward matrix products replace an unqualified backward=2x rule.

sections.heading: Phase 3: Memory traffic analysis (the physics at work)
sections.decision: Matrix-only FLOP counts follow observed operand shapes; logical bytes, HBM traffic, launch events and CPU observations are kept separate. The source's approximate CE/traffic model is not a measured GPU trace.

sections.heading: Phase 4: Hardware abstraction (solving the abstraction problem)
sections.decision: Backend dispatch and explicit shape/arithmetic costs are mapped. The full original 3D placement figure is compared and integrated with the distributed chapter's actual groups, ownership and batch definitions. The example validates logical coordinates, not all backends or hardware execution; no identical-results/all-backends assertion is accepted.

sections.heading: Fallacies and Pitfalls
sections.decision: Accepted S8/S7/AD examples cover dispatch/completion, tracing, AD memory and arithmetic-versus-measurement findings. Actual ONNX/TensorFlow export and complete MLOps comparison now supply portability and selection. Unsupported source performance statements are not promoted to observations.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.decision: Retain the complete source recap in the source layer. Do not duplicate it as a new reader-facing definition page. Mechanism acceptance comes from the separate revision-specific comparisons and examples, not this recap.
